text: A sick bug collector mailed Darwin his own secret theory.
Eighteen fifty-eight, Indonesia. Alfred Wallace is shaking with malaria.
In his fever, an idea hits him: only the best-fitted survive, and species change.
He mails it to Charles Darwin.
Darwin goes pale. He'd hidden that exact idea for twenty years.
"All my originality," he writes, "will be smashed."
So both papers are read together in London.
The room listens. Nobody argues. Nobody notices.
Months later, the club's president calls it a year with no striking discoveries.
Then Darwin's book sells out in a day.
Wallace never complains. He even names his own book Darwinism.
Would you have shared the credit?
